name: application-pos-keypad
title: POS Keypad
description: Point-of-sale numeric amount keypad with quick-cash buttons; cash tendered accumulates digit-by-digit and change due is always computed live from tendered minus the real total.
useWhen: Taking a cash payment in a point-of-sale or checkout terminal UI where a physical keyboard isn't the primary input.
Cashiers benefit from quick-cash shortcut buttons for common tender amounts instead of typing every digit.
Change due should be visibly computed and updated as digits are entered, not calculated only after submission.
avoidWhen: You need a generic numeric stepper for product quantity — use `quantity-inputs` for that increment/decrement pattern instead.
Payment is card-only with no cash tendered/change flow — a simpler total display is enough.
The amount should be freely editable text rather than append-only digit entry — use a plain currency input instead.
responsiveBehavior: Fixed-width card (max-w-xs) sized for a checkout terminal; keypad buttons remain in a fixed 3-column grid at all widths.
accessibility: Change due and cash tendered are both derived from the same accumulated cents value and the real total prop, so they can never disagree.
The Charge button is a real disabled <button> when tendered cash is short of the total, not just visually dimmed.
Change due switches between emerald (covered) and red (short) together with the numeric sign, never relying on color alone.

variants.title: POS Keypad
variants.description: Total due $18.50 with quick-cash buttons for $20/$25/$40 and a full numeric keypad; change due updates live as digits are entered.
accessibility: Change due is recomputed from the same tendered/total values on every keypad press, verified interactively.

variants.title: POS Keypad (Dark)
variants.description: POS keypad adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Change due and keypad button colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
